content: Live-verified (curl) both Cloudflare (https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=X&type=Y with header 'accept: application/dns-json') and Google (https://dns.google/resolve?name=X&type=Y, no special header needed) return 'access-control-allow-origin: *' - both are directly callable from browser JS with zero proxy/CORS workaround needed. Both use the same de-facto JSON schema (Status/TC/RD/RA/AD/CD/Question/Answer array with name/type/TTL/data), Status field uses standard DNS RCODE numbers (0=NOERROR,3=NXDOMAIN) confirmed via live NXDOMAIN test. Cloudflare's indicative rate limit is ~1000 req/hour/IP (informal, generous for a low-traffic tool site); Google's is <1500 QPS/IP (also generous). No official DoH JSON RFC exists - behavior can diverge across providers, but both tested providers matched on schema in practice. Quad9's DoH JSON GET endpoint did not respond on the tested path (needs a different endpoint verification).
